question: A team pastes each Claude-written summary into a second Claude conversation and asks it to flag any invented claims. The second conversation is not given the underlying documents. What is the greatest risk?
options: A) The second conversation will refuse the request because it cannot see the original documents.
B) Without the source material the checker can only judge plausibility, so invented claims pass.
C) The second conversation consumes so much allowance that the team runs out before finishing.
D) The checker will rewrite the summary instead of assessing it, so the wording changes each time.
correct_answers: B) Without the source material the checker can only judge plausibility, so invented claims pass.
explanations: Incorrect. It will answer willingly, which is what makes the arrangement misleading rather than merely useless.
Correct. A check with no access to the evidence can assess whether a claim sounds reasonable, and a fabricated claim was generated precisely because it sounds reasonable.
Incorrect. The extra cost is real but modest, and it is not what makes this practice unsafe.
Incorrect. Rewriting is easy to notice and easy to correct. The damaging failure is a confident clearance the team believes.
